morning_d1.text: Gannet Rock, this is Station Rockland. Radio check. Tide's dropping fast; if you want the outer stacks before noon, now's your window.
morning_d1.speaker: clara

options.text: Copy, Clara. Lamp's steady, weights are wound. Heading out.
options.reply: Roger. Give me a shout if anything strange washed up in last night's squall.

options.text: Copy. I'll look around and radio if I find anything worth your time.
options.reply: Worth my time is a low bar out here, Arthur. Anything you find, I'd like to hear about.

react_east_bar_first.text: Careful crossing that bar, Arthur. Keep one eye on your pocket watch so you make it back before high tide.
react_east_bar_first.speaker: clara

react_west_bar_first.text: West bar's narrower than the east, and it floods first. Mind the gulleys.
react_west_bar_first.speaker: clara

react_bar_rising.text: Water's making, Arthur. You've maybe an hour of crossing left.
react_bar_rising.speaker: clara

react_bar_closing.text: Arthur, get off that bar. Now. I mean it.
react_bar_closing.speaker: clara

react_west_withheld.text: You're out on the west stack. Is there anything about the east stack you'd like to tell me?
react_west_withheld.speaker: clara

options.text: There was a canister in the hull. PROJECT PELAGIC, 1974. I should have said.
options.reply: Yes. You should have. Thank you for saying it now.
All right. Whenever you're ready.

react_cottage_curious.text: Sounds quiet in there. Are you eating properly, Arthur?
react_cottage_curious.speaker: clara

shipwreck.text: You walked all the way out to the East Stack. What did you find wedged in the hull?
shipwreck.speaker: clara

options.text: An orange canister stamped 'PROJECT PELAGIC, 1974'. It's in the satchel.
options.reply: ...Keep it dry, and bring it back before the bar floods. Don't open it out in the salt spray.

options.text: Old trawler wreck, Clara. Nothing worth reporting.
options.reply: Mm. Watch the water behind you; that bar vanishes fast.

seacave.text: Echo Cave? Your signal's bouncing off the walls. What's sitting in the arch?
seacave.speaker: clara

options.text: A rusted acoustic buoy. The casing is warm, and there's a cassette taped inside the hatch.
options.reply: Warm? ...Nobody's serviced those buoys since the station closed. Bring the tape home, Arthur, and head for high ground.

options.text: Just kelp and barnacles. Eerie acoustics.
options.reply: Don't linger. The Atlantic doesn't wait for sightseers.

evening_d1.text: The beam looks beautiful from here. Thank you for telling me about that canister, Arthur. I know it isn't easy, handing over odd things you find.
evening_d1.speaker: clara

options.text: It said PROJECT PELAGIC on the side. Does that mean anything to you?
options.reply: ...Not tonight. I'll tell you what I can, when I can.
Then you're better at it than the last three keepers.

evening_d1.text: Lamp's turning well. You were out on the east stack a long time today. Anything you'd care to tell me?
evening_d1.speaker: clara

options.text: There was a canister in the hull. PROJECT PELAGIC, 1974. I should have said.
options.reply: Yes. You should have. Thank you for saying it now.
All right, Arthur. Goodnight.

evening_d1.text: Beam's turning pretty from here. How was your first day on the rock, really?
evening_d1.speaker: clara

options.text: Lonelier than I expected. But I like it.
options.reply: That's honest. Most keepers say it takes three days to stop listening for company.
All business. Fine. Get some sleep, Arthur.

morning_d2.text: Morning, Arthur. Slept better than I have in weeks, knowing someone out there tells me the truth. How's the rock?
morning_d2.speaker: clara

options.text: Quiet night. Where do you want me today?
options.reply: West stack, if the water allows. The old echo cave. Mind the tide table.

options.text: That canister's still on my mind.
options.reply: Leave it dry and don't pry at it. I mean that kindly.

morning_d2.text: Morning. Fog's lifting a little. Arthur, I'd rather you were straight with me about what's out there.
morning_d2.speaker: clara

options.reply: That's all I ask.
Then do it well.

morning_d2.text: Morning, Arthur. Flat calm and grey out here. Anything strange wash up overnight?
morning_d2.speaker: clara

options.reply: Good. Keep it that way.
Leave it dry and don't pry at it. I mean that kindly.

evening_d2.text: You've been quiet all evening. Did you play the tape?
evening_d2.speaker: clara

options.text: Walt was talking to his wife. June. He said the Navy lied about the cable job.
options.reply: ...Yes. I know the name. Let me tell you about it, another night.
Static and wind. Of course.

evening_d2.text: Did you find a tape out there? You've got a cassette player in the cottage.
evening_d2.speaker: clara

options.reply: Do. And tell me what's on it.
...All right.

evening_d2.text: How was the day, Arthur? You sound far away.
evening_d2.speaker: clara

options.text: Tired. The rock's getting to me.
options.reply: It does that. Sleep.
Goodnight, then.

cable.text: North cove? That's the old cable landing. The charts show a line coming ashore there. What's it look like?
cable.speaker: clara

options.text: An armored cable running straight into the sea. Brass tag: PELAGIC, ARRAY 2, USN.
options.reply: ...Then the charts weren't wrong. Leave the hut alone, Arthur, and don't touch the splice.
All right. Mind the tide on the way back.

vault.text: The reef is open? I can hear the water around you. What's down there?
vault.speaker: clara

options.text: A cable vault. Salt-crusted hatch, and a field recorder wedged behind the ladder. Initials: J.H.
options.reply: ...Bring it up. Please. Then get off the reef.
Then come home.

react_north_cove_first.text: North cove. Careful on the shingle; it's slick, and the water floods that bar before the others.
react_north_cove_first.speaker: clara

react_south_reef_first.text: The reef! I never thought the water dropped that far. You have an hour at best, Arthur.
react_south_reef_first.speaker: clara

react_reef_closing.text: The water's turned on the reef. Get off it. Now.
react_reef_closing.speaker: clara

evening_d3.text: You found the north landing and you told me. I won't forget that, Arthur.
evening_d3.speaker: clara

options.reply: ...Another night. I promise.
Then the job's in good hands.

evening_d3.text: You were in the north cove a long time. Is there something you'd like to say?
evening_d3.speaker: clara

options.text: There's a cable, and a brass tag. PELAGIC ARRAY 2. I should have said.
options.reply: Yes. You should have. Thank you.
All right.

evening_d3.text: Found anything in the north cove? The old charts show a cable there.
evening_d3.speaker: clara

options.text: Haven't made it up there yet.
options.reply: Fog's thick today. Wait for a clear low.
Alright, Arthur.

evening_d5.text: You brought it up. Thank you, Arthur. I couldn't have gone down there.
evening_d5.speaker: clara

options.reply: ...Play it tonight. Then I'll answer anything you ask.

options.text: June was careful. She wasn't careless.
options.reply: No. She wasn't.

evening_d5.text: You were on the reef longer than the table allowed. What did you find?
evening_d5.speaker: clara

options.text: A recorder. A cassette, initials J.H. I'm sorry I said nothing.
options.reply: Thank you for telling me now.
...All right.

evening_d5.text: You didn't make the reef today? That low won't come again this winter.
evening_d5.speaker: clara

options.reply: It will be gone by then.
Maybe not.

lines.text: [Click. Tape hiss. Wind against the microphone.]
June. It's the nineteenth. The array's quiet tonight, so I thought I'd talk to you instead of the log.
The Navy men left on the Tuesday boat. They took the good coffee and left me the paperwork.
I walked out to the stack this morning at low water. Your buoy's still ticking away in the arch, warm as a loaf. I don't think I'll ever get used to that.
I keep telling myself you'd laugh at me, talking to a machine.
They tell me you were never on the manifest. That there was no cable job that night. I've read their letter four times and I still don't believe it.
[Click. Rushing water. A metal hatch clangs. Breathing.]
Field recorder, J. Haskell, November the fourth. Cable vault, south reef. Splice number two has been dropping signal for a week, and the Navy wants it fixed before the weather turns.
The tide table says I have an hour of low water. The Navy's schedule says two. I'm going with the table. Walt, if you're listening to this over your coffee, I know, I know.
It's cold down here. The hatch seal's salt-crusted solid. The whole vault smells of iron and old rope.
[Water against the hatch.] That's... earlier than the table said. Well. I'll finish the splice and be out before it matters.
If this recorder ever ends up on someone else's shelf: tell Walt, the left pocket. He'll know.
